question: Which of the following is a folk dance of Haryana?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ghoomar**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• **Ghoomar** is a highly popular folk dance performed in **Haryana**, particularly in the regions adjoining **Rajasthan** such as **Bhiwani**, **Hisar**, **Rohtak**, and **Sirsa**.

• The dance is exclusively performed by **women** who wear traditional colorful costumes including the **Ghagra** (a long flared skirt) and a veil, creating a vibrant visual display as they twirl.

• The term is derived from the word **ghoomna**, which signifies the graceful **circular movements** and pirouettes executed by the dancers while moving in a clockwise and anti-clockwise direction.

• It is typically showcased during significant cultural festivals such as **Holi**, **Gangaur**, and **Teej**, as well as during **wedding ceremonies** to celebrate fertility and joy.

• While it shares its name and core style with the state dance of **Rajasthan**, the Haryanvi version has distinct local variations in **rhythm** and **folk songs**.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Garba**:

• A traditional dance form originating from the state of **Gujarat**.

• It is primarily performed during the nine nights of the **Navratri** festival to honor **Goddess Durga**.

• **Kuchipudi**:

• One of the **eight classical dances** of India, originating from the **Andhra Pradesh** state.

• It uniquely combines **dance**, **gestures**, **speech**, and **song**, often based on **mythological** themes.

• **Gidda**:

• A lively and energetic folk dance of **Punjab**, performed by **women**.

• It is characterized by rhythmic **clapping** and the singing of **bolis** (short folk verses) reflecting daily life and social issues.

• **Other Folk Dances of Haryana**:

• **Phag Dance**: Performed by farmers in the month of **Phalguna** to celebrate the harvest.

• **Loor**: Popular in the **Bangar** area, performed by girls during the spring season.

• **Daph Dance**: A seasonal dance performed to the accompaniment of the **Daph** (drum).
